moat_against: Smallest of the Big Three core providers — Fiserv and FIS have far greater scale and R&D budgets
Structural client shrinkage: US bank and credit-union consolidation deletes a customer at every merger; deconversion fees are one-time, the recurring revenue is gone
Moat maintenance is expensive and rising: capitalized software development of $167.2M (FY24), $172.4M (FY25), $184.2M (FY26) — roughly 3x the PP&E capex the engine deducts
Cloud-native and modular challengers (nCino, Mambu, Temenos, fintech point solutions) unbundle pieces of the stack, especially digital and payments
Served market grows slowly: revenue CAGR ~7% over 5 years, FY27 guided to +5.5-6.5%; concentrated in US community/regional institutions with no geographic diversification
moat_for: Mission-critical core platforms (Jack Henry Core for banks, Symitar for credit unions) — a core conversion is the highest-risk project a bank runs; multi-year contracts, very low churn
ROIC proxy 19.2-25.2% every year FY17-FY26 (23.5% FY26; management-reported ROIC 23.2%) — returns stayed well above the cost of capital through COVID and the 2023 bank stress
Integrated stack raises switching costs with each product: Core 30.2% of FY26 revenue, Payments 36.8%, Complementary 29.6%, plus Banno digital banking
Record 58 competitive core wins in FY26, 14 at institutions over $1B in assets — taking share from Fiserv/FIS, not just defending the base
Gross margin 41-44% for a decade (43.7% FY26) and operating margin back to 25.0% — pricing power without margin erosion
moat_justification: Mission-critical core processing with very high switching costs and a decade of ROIC proxy at 19-25% (23.5% in FY26), but the smallest of the Big Three core providers, a structurally shrinking US bank/credit-union client base, and moat maintenance that costs $167-184M/yr of capitalized software development.
name: Jack Henry & Associates, Inc.
one_liner: High-quality core-banking franchise, moat 7/10 — does not clear 15% at $153.19 (weighted IRR 10.1%, IV@15 $88.34; clears 15% only below ~$88) and the scored OE excludes $167-184M/yr of capitalized software development, so the printed IRR is an upper bound.
